rows.jp: 学校に来る理由もない。当然か。
rows.en: She has no reason to come to school. Of course.

ghs.en: Obviously. She has no reason to come to school either.

rows.jp: 少しばかり物足りない。

ghs.en: A bit and no more of dissatisfaction.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that something feels a little lacking or unsatisfying. The English is an ungrammatical noun fragment and adds the unsupported limit 'and no more.'

highlights.text: A bit and no more of dissatisfaction.

rows.jp: 少しばかり自分の席に座ってみる。
rows.en: Just for a little while, I sit at my desk.

ghs.en: A while and no more I try to sit down in my seat.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that he tries sitting in his own seat for a little while. The English uses inverted word order and again invents 'and no more.'

highlights.text: A while and no more I try to sit down in my seat.

rows.jp: 少しばかり、物思いにふけってみる。
rows.en: Just for a little while, I let myself sink into thought.

ghs.en: I will try to lose myself in reverie, a while and no more.
ghs.assessment: 少しばかり means 'for a little while'; it does not insist 'and no more,' and the phrase is misplaced after the object.
